what does digitalread do in arduino | arduino digitalread | how do i use digitalread on arduino | digitalread arduino explained => In Arduino, `digitalRead()` reads the value from a specified digital pin, either `HIGH` or `LOW`. Use it like `digitalRead(pin)`.
what are the parameters of digitalread arduino | what goes inside digitalread arduino => In Arduino, `digitalRead()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin number you want to read.
what does digitalwrite do in arduino | arduino digitalwrite | how do i use digitalwrite on arduino | digitalwrite arduino explained => Write a `HIGH` or a `LOW` value to a digital pin. If the pin has been configured as an `OUTPUT` with `pinMode()`, its voltage will be set to the corresponding value: 5V (or 3.3V on 3.3V boards) for `HIGH`, 0V (ground) for `LOW`. Use it like `digitalWrite(pin, value)`.
what does digitalwrite return in arduino | arduino digitalwrite return value => In Arduino, `digitalWrite()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of digitalwrite arduino | what goes inside digitalwrite arduino => In Arduino, `digitalWrite()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin number. `value`: `HIGH` or `LOW`.
what does pinmode do in arduino | arduino pinmode | how do i use pinmode on arduino | pinmode arduino explained => In Arduino, `pinMode()` configures the specified pin to behave either as an input or an output. Use it like `pinMode(pin, mode)`.
what does pinmode return in arduino | arduino pinmode return value => In Arduino, `pinMode()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of pinmode arduino | what goes inside pinmode arduino => In Arduino, `pinMode()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin number to set the mode of. `mode`: `INPUT`, `OUTPUT`, or `INPUT_PULLUP`.
what does analogread do in arduino | arduino analogread | how do i use analogread on arduino | analogread arduino explained => In Arduino, `analogRead()` reads the value from the specified analog pin. Arduino boards contain a multichannel, 10-bit analog to digital converter. This means that it will map input voltages between 0 and the operating voltage(5V or 3.3V) into integer values between 0 and 1023. Use it like `analogRead(pin)`.
what does analogread return in arduino | arduino analogread return value => In Arduino, `analogRead()` returns the analog reading on the pin. Although it is limited to the resolution of the analog to digital converter (0-1023 for 10 bits or 0-4095 for 12 bits). Data type: `int`.
what are the parameters of analogread arduino | what goes inside analogread arduino => In Arduino, `analogRead()` takes: `pin`: the name of the analog input pin to read from.
what does analogreadresolution do in arduino | arduino analogreadresolution | how do i use analogreadresolution on arduino | analogreadresolution arduino explained => In Arduino, `analogReadResolution()` is an extension of the Analog API for the Zero, Due, MKR family, Nano 33 (BLE and IoT) and Portenta. Sets the size (in bits) of the value returned by `analogRead()`. It defaults to 10 bits (returns values between 0-1023) for backward compatibility with AVR based boards. Use it like `analogReadResolution(bits)`.
what does analogreadresolution return in arduino | arduino analogreadresolution return value => In Arduino, `analogReadResolution()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of analogreadresolution arduino | what goes inside analogreadresolution arduino => In Arduino, `analogReadResolution()` takes: `bits`: determines the resolution (in bits) of the value returned by the `analogRead()` function. You can set this between 1 and 32. You can set resolutions higher than the supported 12 or 16 bits, but values returned by `analogRead()` will suffer approximation.
what does analogreference do in arduino | arduino analogreference | how do i use analogreference on arduino | analogreference arduino explained => In Arduino, `analogReference()` configures the reference voltage used for analog input (that is the value used as the top of the input range). Use it like `analogReference(type)`.
what does analogreference return in arduino | arduino analogreference return value => In Arduino, `analogReference()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does analogwrite do in arduino | arduino analogwrite | how do i use analogwrite on arduino | analogwrite arduino explained => In Arduino, `analogWrite()` writes an analog value (PWM wave) to a pin. Can be used to light a LED at varying brightnesses or drive a motor at various speeds. Use it like `analogWrite(pin, value)`.
what does analogwrite return in arduino | arduino analogwrite return value => In Arduino, `analogWrite()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of analogwrite arduino | what goes inside analogwrite arduino => In Arduino, `analogWrite()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin to write to. Allowed data types: `int`. `value`: the duty cycle: between 0 (always off) and 255 (always on). Allowed data types: `int`.
what does analogwriteresolution do in arduino | arduino analogwriteresolution | how do i use analogwriteresolution on arduino | analogwriteresolution arduino explained => In Arduino, `analogWriteResolution()` is an extension of the Analog API for the Arduino Due. `analogWriteResolution()` sets the resolution of the `analogWrite()` function. It defaults to 8 bits (values between 0-255) for backward compatibility with AVR based boards. Use it like `analogWriteResolution(bits)`.
what does analogwriteresolution return in arduino | arduino analogwriteresolution return value => In Arduino, `analogWriteResolution()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of analogwriteresolution arduino | what goes inside analogwriteresolution arduino => In Arduino, `analogWriteResolution()` takes: `bits`: determines the resolution (in bits) of the values used in the `analogWrite()` function. The value can range from 1 to 32. If you choose a resolution higher or lower than your board's hardware capabilities, the value used in `analogWrite()` will be either truncated if it's too high or padded with zeros if it's too low.
what does notone do in arduino | arduino notone | how do i use notone on arduino | notone arduino explained => In Arduino, `noTone()` stops the generation of a square wave triggered by `tone()`. Has no effect if no tone is being generated. Use it like `noTone(pin)`.
what does notone return in arduino | arduino notone return value => In Arduino, `noTone()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of notone arduino | what goes inside notone arduino => In Arduino, `noTone()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin on which to stop generating the tone.
what does pulsein do in arduino | arduino pulsein | how do i use pulsein on arduino | pulsein arduino explained => In Arduino, `pulseIn()` reads a pulse (either `HIGH` or `LOW`) on a pin. Use it like `pulseIn(pin, value)`.
what does pulsein return in arduino | arduino pulsein return value => In Arduino, `pulseIn()` returns the length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout. Data type: `unsigned long`.
what are the parameters of pulsein arduino | what goes inside pulsein arduino => In Arduino, `pulseIn()` takes: `pin`: the number of the Arduino pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: `int`. `value`: type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: `int`. `timeout` (optional): the number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: `unsigned long`.
what does pulseinlong do in arduino | arduino pulseinlong | how do i use pulseinlong on arduino | pulseinlong arduino explained => In Arduino, `pulseInLong()` is an alternative to pulseIn() which is better at handling long pulse and interrupt affected scenarios. Reads a pulse (either `HIGH` or `LOW`) on a pin. Use it like `pulseInLong(pin, value)`.
what does pulseinlong return in arduino | arduino pulseinlong return value => In Arduino, `pulseInLong()` returns the length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout. Data type: `unsigned long`.
what are the parameters of pulseinlong arduino | what goes inside pulseinlong arduino => In Arduino, `pulseInLong()` takes: `pin`: the number of the Arduino pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: `int`. `value`: type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: `int`. `timeout` (optional): the number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: `unsigned long`.
what does shiftin do in arduino | arduino shiftin | how do i use shiftin on arduino | shiftin arduino explained => In Arduino, `shiftIn()` shifts in a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (that is the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. For each bit, the clock pin is pulled high, the next bit is read from the data line, and then the clock pin is taken low. Use it like `byte incoming = shiftIn(dataPin, clockPin, bitOrder)`.
what does shiftin return in arduino | arduino shiftin return value => In Arduino, `shiftIn()` returns the value read. Data type: `byte`.
what are the parameters of shiftin arduino | what goes inside shiftin arduino => In Arduino, `shiftIn()` takes: `dataPin`: the pin on which to input each bit. Allowed data types: `int`. `clockPin`: the pin to toggle to signal a read from dataPin. `bitOrder`: which order to shift in the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).
what does shiftout do in arduino | arduino shiftout | how do i use shiftout on arduino | shiftout arduino explained => In Arduino, `shiftOut()` shifts out a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (that is the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. Each bit is written in turn to a data pin, after which a clock pin is pulsed (taken high, then low) to indicate that the bit is available. Use it like `shiftOut(dataPin, clockPin, bitOrder, value)`.
what does shiftout return in arduino | arduino shiftout return value => In Arduino, `shiftOut()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of shiftout arduino | what goes inside shiftout arduino => In Arduino, `shiftOut()` takes: `dataPin`: the pin on which to output each bit. Allowed data types: `int`. `clockPin`: the pin to toggle once the dataPin has been set to the correct value. Allowed data types: `int`. `bitOrder`: which order to shift out the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).
what does tone do in arduino | arduino tone | how do i use tone on arduino | tone arduino explained => In Arduino, `tone()` generates a square wave of the specified frequency (and 50% duty cycle) on a pin. A duration can be specified, otherwise the wave continues until a call to noTone(). The pin can be connected to a piezo buzzer or other speaker to play tones. Only one tone can be generated at a time. Use it like `tone(pin, frequency)`.
what does tone return in arduino | arduino tone return value => In Arduino, `tone()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of tone arduino | what goes inside tone arduino => In Arduino, `tone()` takes: `pin`: the Arduino pin on which to generate the tone. `frequency`: the frequency of the tone in hertz. Allowed data types: `unsigned int`. `duration`: the duration of the tone in milliseconds (optional). Allowed data types: `unsigned long`.
what does delay do in arduino | arduino delay | how do i use delay on arduino | delay arduino explained => In Arduino, `delay()` pauses the program for the amount of time (in milliseconds) specified as parameter. (There are 1000 milliseconds in a second.) Use it like `delay(ms)`.
what does delay return in arduino | arduino delay return value => In Arduino, `delay()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of delay arduino | what goes inside delay arduino => In Arduino, `delay()` takes: `ms`: the number of milliseconds to pause. Allowed data types: `unsigned long`.
what does delaymicroseconds do in arduino | arduino delaymicroseconds | how do i use delaymicroseconds on arduino | delaymicroseconds arduino explained => In Arduino, `delayMicroseconds()` pauses the program for the amount of time (in microseconds) specified by the parameter. There are a thousand microseconds in a millisecond and a million microseconds in a second. Use it like `delayMicroseconds(us)`.
what does delaymicroseconds return in arduino | arduino delaymicroseconds return value => In Arduino, `delayMicroseconds()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of delaymicroseconds arduino | what goes inside delaymicroseconds arduino => In Arduino, `delayMicroseconds()` takes: `us`: the number of microseconds to pause. Allowed data types: `unsigned int`.
what does micros do in arduino | arduino micros | how do i use micros on arduino | micros arduino explained => In Arduino, `micros()` returns the number of microseconds since the Arduino board began running the program. This number will overflow (go back to zero), after approximately 70 minutes. On the boards from the Arduino Portenta family this function has a resolution of one microsecond on all cores. Use it like `time = micros()`.
what does millis do in arduino | arduino millis | how do i use millis on arduino | millis arduino explained => In Arduino, `millis()` returns the number of milliseconds passed since the Arduino board began running the program. This number will overflow (go back to zero), after approximately 50 days. Use it like `time = millis()`.
what does millis return in arduino | arduino millis return value => In Arduino, `millis()` returns number of milliseconds passed since the program started. Data type: `unsigned long`.
what does abs do in arduino | arduino abs | how do i use abs on arduino | abs arduino explained => In Arduino, `abs()` calculates the absolute value of a number. Use it like `abs(x)`.
what does constrain do in arduino | arduino constrain | how do i use constrain on arduino | constrain arduino explained => In Arduino, `constrain()` constrains a number to be within a range. Use it like `constrain(x, a, b)`.
what does constrain return in arduino | arduino constrain return value => In Arduino, `constrain()` returns x: if x is between a and b. a: if x is less than a. b: if x is greater than b.
what are the parameters of constrain arduino | what goes inside constrain arduino => In Arduino, `constrain()` takes: `x`: the number to constrain Allowed data types: all data types. `a`: the lower end of the range. Allowed data types: all data types. `b`: the upper end of the range. Allowed data types: all data types.
what does map do in arduino | arduino map | how do i use map on arduino | map arduino explained => In Arduino, `map()` re-maps a number from one range to another. That is, a value of fromLow would get mapped to toLow, a value of fromHigh to toHigh, values in-between to values in-between, and so on. Does not constrain values to within the range, because out-of-range values are sometimes intended and useful. Use it like `map(value, fromLow, fromHigh, toLow, toHigh)`.
what does map return in arduino | arduino map return value => In Arduino, `map()` returns the mapped value. Data type: `long`.
what are the parameters of map arduino | what goes inside map arduino => In Arduino, `map()` takes: `value`: the number to map. `fromLow`: the lower bound of the value's current range. `fromHigh`: the upper bound of the value's current range. `toLow`: the lower bound of the value's target range. `toHigh`: the upper bound of the value's target range.

what are the parameters of max arduino | what goes inside max arduino => In Arduino, `max()` takes: `x`: the first number. Allowed data types: any data type. `y`: the second number. Allowed data types: any data type.

This function is sometimes referred to as an interrupt service routine.

what does digitalpintointerrupt do in arduino | arduino digitalpintointerrupt | how do i use digitalpintointerrupt on arduino | digitalpintointerrupt arduino explained => The `digitalPinToInterrupt()` function takes a pin as an argument, and returns the same pin if it can be used as an interrupt. Use it like `digitalPinToInterrupt(pin)`.
how do i use interrupts on arduino | interrupts arduino explained => In Arduino, `interrupts()` re-enables interrupts (after they've been disabled by noInterrupts(). Interrupts allow certain important tasks to happen in the background and are enabled by default. Some functions will not work while interrupts are disabled, and incoming communication may be ignored. Use it like `interrupts()`.
what does interrupts return in arduino | arduino interrupts return value => In Arduino, `interrupts()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does nointerrupts do in arduino | arduino nointerrupts | how do i use nointerrupts on arduino | nointerrupts arduino explained => In Arduino, `noInterrupts()` disables interrupts (you can re-enable them with `interrupts()`). Interrupts allow certain important tasks to happen in the background and are enabled by default. Some functions will not work while interrupts are disabled, and incoming communication may be ignored. Use it like `noInterrupts()`.
what does nointerrupts return in arduino | arduino nointerrupts return value => In Arduino, `noInterrupts()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what is serial in arduino | arduino serial library | serial object arduino => Used for communication between the Arduino board and a computer or other devices.
what is wire in arduino | arduino wire library | wire object arduino => This library allows you to communicate with I2C devices, a feature that is present on all Arduino boards. I2C is a very common protocol, primarily used for reading/sending data to/from external I2C components.
what is spi in arduino | arduino spi library | spi object arduino => This library allows you to communicate with SPI devices, with the Arduino as the controller device. This library is bundled with every Arduino platform (avr, megaavr, mbed, samd, sam, arc32), so you do not need to install the library separately.
what is stream in arduino | arduino stream library | stream object arduino => Stream is the base class for character and binary based streams. It is not called directly, but invoked whenever you use a function that relies on it. Stream defines the reading functions in Arduino.
arduino keyboard library | keyboard object arduino => The keyboard functions enable 32u4 or SAMD micro based boards to send keystrokes to an attached computer through their micro's native USB port.
what is mouse in arduino | arduino mouse library | mouse object arduino => The mouse functions enable 32u4 or SAMD micro based boards to control cursor movement on a connected computer through their micro's native USB port. When updating the cursor position, it is always relative to the cursor's previous location.
what does serial.available do in arduino | arduino serial.available | how do i use serial.available on arduino | serial.available arduino explained => Get the number of bytes (characters) available for reading from the serial port. This is data that's already arrived and stored in the serial receive buffer (which holds 64 bytes). `Serial.available()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.available()`.
what does serial.available return in arduino | arduino serial.available return value => In Arduino, `Serial.available()` returns the number of bytes available to read.
what does serial.availableforwrite do in arduino | arduino serial.availableforwrite | how do i use serial.availableforwrite on arduino | serial.availableforwrite arduino explained => Get the number of bytes (characters) available for writing in the serial buffer without blocking the write operation. Use it like `Serial.availableForWrite()`.
what does serial.availableforwrite return in arduino | arduino serial.availableforwrite return value => In Arduino, `Serial.availableForWrite()` returns the number of bytes available to write.
what does serial.begin do in arduino | arduino serial.begin | how do i use serial.begin on arduino | serial.begin arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.begin()` sets the data rate in bits per second (baud) for serial data transmission. For communicating with Serial Monitor, make sure to use one of the baud rates listed in the menu at the bottom right corner of its screen. Use it like `Serial.begin(speed)`.
what does serial.begin return in arduino | arduino serial.begin return value => In Arduino, `Serial.begin()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does serial.end do in arduino | arduino serial.end | how do i use serial.end on arduino | serial.end arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.end()` disables serial communication, allowing the RX and TX pins to be used for general input and output. To re-enable serial communication, call Serial.begin(). Use it like `Serial.end()`.
what does serial.end return in arduino | arduino serial.end return value => In Arduino, `Serial.end()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does serial.find do in arduino | arduino serial.find | how do i use serial.find on arduino | serial.find arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.find()` reads data from the serial buffer until the target is found. The function returns `true` if target is found, `false` if it times out. `Serial.find()` inherits from the stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.find(target)`.
what does serial.finduntil do in arduino | arduino serial.finduntil | how do i use serial.finduntil on arduino | serial.finduntil arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.findUntil()` reads data from the serial buffer until a target string of given length or terminator string is found. The function returns true if the target string is found, false if it times out. `Serial.findUntil()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.findUntil(target, terminal)`.
what does serial.flush do in arduino | arduino serial.flush | how do i use serial.flush on arduino | serial.flush arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.flush()` waits for the transmission of outgoing serial data to complete. `flush()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.flush()`.

what does serial.parsefloat do in arduino | arduino serial.parsefloat | how do i use serial.parsefloat on arduino | serial.parsefloat arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.parseFloat()` returns the first valid floating point number from the Serial buffer. `parseFloat()` is terminated by the first character that is not a floating point number. Use it like `Serial.parseFloat()`.
what does serial.parseint do in arduino | arduino serial.parseint | how do i use serial.parseint on arduino | serial.parseint arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.parseInt()` looks for the next valid integer in the incoming serial. Use it like `Serial.parseInt()`.
what does serial.parseint return in arduino | arduino serial.parseint return value => In Arduino, `Serial.parseInt()` returns the next valid integer. Data type: `long`.
what does serial.peek do in arduino | arduino serial.peek | how do i use serial.peek on arduino | serial.peek arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.peek()` returns the next byte (character) of incoming serial data without removing it from the internal serial buffer. That is, successive calls to `peek()` will return the same character, as will the next call to `read()`. `Serial.peek()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.peek()`.
what does serial.peek return in arduino | arduino serial.peek return value => In Arduino, `Serial.peek()` returns the first byte of incoming serial data available (or -1 if no data is available). Data type: `int`.
what does serial.print do in arduino | arduino serial.print | how do i use serial.print on arduino | serial.print arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.print()` prints data to the serial port as human-readable ASCII text. This command can take many forms. Numbers are printed using an ASCII character for each digit. Floats are similarly printed as ASCII digits, defaulting to two decimal places. Bytes are sent as a single character. Use it like `Serial.print(val)`.
what does serial.println do in arduino | arduino serial.println | how do i use serial.println on arduino | serial.println arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.println()` prints data to the serial port as human-readable ASCII text followed by a carriage return character (ASCII 13, or '\r') and a newline character (ASCII 10, or '\n'). This command takes the same forms as Serial.print(). Use it like `Serial.println(val)`.
what does serial.read do in arduino | arduino serial.read | how do i use serial.read on arduino | serial.read arduino explained => In Arduino, `Serial.read()` reads incoming serial data. `Serial.read()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Serial.read()`.
what does serial.read return in arduino | arduino serial.read return value => In Arduino, `Serial.read()` returns the first byte of incoming serial data available (or -1 if no data is available). Data type: `int`.

This data is sent as a byte or series of bytes; to send the characters representing the digits of a number use the print() function instead. Use it like `Serial.write(val)`.

how do i use if serial on arduino | if serial arduino explained => In Arduino, `if (Serial)` indicates if the specified Serial port is ready. On the boards with native USB, `if (Serial)` (or `if(SerialUSB)` on the Due) indicates whether or not the USB CDC serial connection is open. For all other boards, and the non-USB CDC ports, this will always return true. Use it like `if (Serial)`.

This function should normally be called only once. Use it like `Wire.begin()`.

what does wire.end return in arduino | arduino wire.end return value => In Arduino, `Wire.end()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does wire.requestfrom do in arduino | arduino wire.requestfrom | how do i use wire.requestfrom on arduino | wire.requestfrom arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.requestFrom()` is used by the controller device to request bytes from a peripheral device. The bytes may then be retrieved with the `available()` and `read()` functions. The `requestFrom()` method accepts a boolean argument changing its behavior for compatibility with certain I2C devices. Use it like `Wire.requestFrom(address, quantity)`.
what does wire.begintransmission do in arduino | arduino wire.begintransmission | how do i use wire.begintransmission on arduino | wire.begintransmission arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.beginTransmission()` begins a transmission to the I2C peripheral device with the given address. Subsequently, queue bytes for transmission with the `write()` function and transmit them by calling `endTransmission()`. Use it like `Wire.beginTransmission(address)`.
what does wire.begintransmission return in arduino | arduino wire.begintransmission return value => In Arduino, `Wire.beginTransmission()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does wire.endtransmission do in arduino | arduino wire.endtransmission | how do i use wire.endtransmission on arduino | wire.endtransmission arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.endTransmission()` ends a transmission to a peripheral device that was begun by `beginTransmission()` and transmits the bytes that were queued by `write()`. The `endTransmission()` method accepts a boolean argument changing its behavior for compatibility with certain I2C devices. Use it like `Wire.endTransmission()`.
what does wire.write do in arduino | arduino wire.write | how do i use wire.write on arduino | wire.write arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.write()` writes data from a peripheral device in response to a request from a controller device, or queues bytes for transmission from a controller to peripheral device (in-between calls to `beginTransmission()` and `endTransmission()`). Use it like `Wire.write(value)`.
what does wire.write return in arduino | arduino wire.write return value => In Arduino, `Wire.write()` returns the number of bytes written (reading this number is optional).
what does wire.available do in arduino | arduino wire.available | how do i use wire.available on arduino | wire.available arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.available()` returns the number of bytes available for retrieval with `read()`. This function should be called on a controller device after a call to `requestFrom()` or on a peripheral inside the `onReceive()` handler. `available()` inherits from the Stream utility class. Use it like `Wire.available()`.
what does wire.available return in arduino | arduino wire.available return value => In Arduino, `Wire.available()` returns the number of bytes available for reading.

Use it like `Wire.read()`.
what does wire.read return in arduino | arduino wire.read return value => In Arduino, `Wire.read()` returns the next byte received.
what does wire.setclock do in arduino | arduino wire.setclock | how do i use wire.setclock on arduino | wire.setclock arduino explained => In Arduino, `Wire.setClock()` modifies the clock frequency for I2C communication. I2C peripheral devices have no minimum working clock frequency, however 100KHz is usually the baseline. Use it like `Wire.setClock(clockFrequency)`.

what does spi.begin do in arduino | arduino spi.begin | how do i use spi.begin on arduino | spi.begin arduino explained => In Arduino, `SPI.begin()` initializes the SPI bus by setting SCK, MOSI, and SS to outputs, pulling SCK and MOSI low, and SS high. Use it like `SPI.begin()`.

Note that calling SPI.begin() is required before calling this one. Use it like `SPI.beginTransaction(mySettings)`.
what does spi.begintransaction return in arduino | arduino spi.begintransaction return value => In Arduino, `SPI.beginTransaction()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does spi.endtransaction do in arduino | arduino spi.endtransaction | how do i use spi.endtransaction on arduino | spi.endtransaction arduino explained => Stop using the SPI bus. Normally this is called after de-asserting the chip select, to allow other libraries to use the SPI bus. Use it like `SPI.endTransaction()`.
what does spi.endtransaction return in arduino | arduino spi.endtransaction return value => In Arduino, `SPI.endTransaction()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does spi.transfer do in arduino | arduino spi.transfer | how do i use spi.transfer on arduino | spi.transfer arduino explained => SPI transfer is based on a simultaneous send and receive: the received data is returned in receivedVal (or receivedVal16). In case of buffer transfers the received data is stored in the buffer in-place (the old data is replaced with the data received). Use it like `receivedVal = SPI.transfer(val)`.
what does spi.transfer return in arduino | arduino spi.transfer return value => In Arduino, `SPI.transfer()` returns the received data.
what does spi.usinginterrupt do in arduino | arduino spi.usinginterrupt | how do i use spi.usinginterrupt on arduino | spi.usinginterrupt arduino explained => If your program will perform SPI transactions within an interrupt, call this function to register the interrupt number or name with the SPI library. This allows `SPI.beginTransaction()` to prevent usage conflicts. Use it like `SPI.usingInterrupt(interruptNumber)`.
what does spi.usinginterrupt return in arduino | arduino spi.usinginterrupt return value => In Arduino, `SPI.usingInterrupt()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of spi.usinginterrupt arduino | what goes inside spi.usinginterrupt arduino => For `SPI.usingInterrupt()`: interruptNumber: the associated interrupt number.
what does spisettings do in arduino | arduino spisettings | how do i use spisettings on arduino | spisettings arduino explained => The `SPISettings` object is used to configure the SPI port for your SPI device. All 3 parameters are combined to a single `SPISettings` object, which is given to `SPI.beginTransaction()`. When all of your settings are constants, SPISettings should be used directly in `SPI.beginTransaction()`. Use it like `SPI.beginTransaction(SPISettings(14000000, MSBFIRST, SPI_MODE0))`.
what does spisettings return in arduino | arduino spisettings return value => In Arduino, `SPISettings` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what are the parameters of spisettings arduino | what goes inside spisettings arduino => In Arduino, `SPISettings` takes: `speedMaximum`: The maximum speed of communication. For a SPI chip rated up to 20 MHz, use 20000000. `dataOrder`: MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST `dataMode`: SPI_MODE0, SPI_MODE1, SPI_MODE2, or SPI_MODE3.

The motion onscreen is always relative to the cursor's current location. Before using `Mouse.move()` you must call Mouse.begin(). Use it like `Mouse.move(xVal, yVal, wheel)`.

what are the parameters of mouse.move arduino | what goes inside mouse.move arduino => In Arduino, `Mouse.move()` takes: `xVal`: amount to move along the x-axis. Allowed data types: `signed char`. `yVal`: amount to move along the y-axis. Allowed data types: `signed char`. `wheel`: amount to move scroll wheel. Allowed data types: `signed char`.
what does mouse.press do in arduino | arduino mouse.press | how do i use mouse.press on arduino | mouse.press arduino explained => In Arduino, `Mouse.press()` sends a button press to a connected computer. A press is the equivalent of clicking and continuously holding the mouse button. A press is cancelled with Mouse.release(). Before using `Mouse.press()`, you need to start communication with Mouse.begin(). `Mouse.press()` defaults to a left button press. Use it like `Mouse.press()`.
what does mouse.press return in arduino | arduino mouse.press return value => In Arduino, `Mouse.press()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what does mouse.release do in arduino | arduino mouse.release | how do i use mouse.release on arduino | mouse.release arduino explained => In Arduino, `Mouse.release()` sends a message that a previously pressed button (invoked through Mouse.press()) is released. `Mouse.release()` defaults to the left button. Use it like `Mouse.release()`.
what does mouse.release return in arduino | arduino mouse.release return value => In Arduino, `Mouse.release()` returns nothing, it just does its job.
what is floating point constants in arduino | arduino floating point constants | how does floating point constants work in arduino code => Similar to integer constants, floating point constants are used to make code more readable. Floating point constants are swapped at compile time for the value to which the expression evaluates.
what is integer constants in arduino | arduino integer constants | how does integer constants work in arduino code => Integer constants are numbers that are used directly in a sketch, like 123.

what is array in arduino | arduino array | how does array work in arduino code => An array is a collection of variables that are accessed with an index number. Arrays in the C++ programming language Arduino sketches are written in can be complicated, but using simple arrays is relatively straightforward.
what is bool in arduino | arduino bool | how does bool work in arduino code => A `bool` holds one of two values, `true` or `false`. (Each `bool` variable occupies one byte of memory.)
what is boolean in arduino | arduino boolean | how does boolean work in arduino code => In Arduino, `boolean` is a non-standard type alias for `bool` defined by Arduino. It's recommended to instead use the standard type `bool`, which is identical.
what is double in arduino | arduino double | how does double work in arduino code => Double precision floating point number. On the Uno and other ATMEGA based boards, this occupies 4 bytes. That is, the double implementation is exactly the same as the float, with no gain in precision. On the Arduino Due, doubles have 8-byte (64 bit) precision.
what is short in arduino | arduino short | how does short work in arduino code => A short is a 16-bit data-type. On all Arduinos (ATMega and ARM based) a short stores a 16-bit (2-byte) value. This yields a range of -32,768 to 32,767 (minimum value of -2 to the power of 15 and a maximum value of (2 to the power of 15) - 1).
what is size_t in arduino | arduino size_t | how does size_t work in arduino code => In Arduino, `size_t` is a data type capable of representing the size of any object in bytes. Examples of the use of `size_t` are the return type of `sizeof()` and `Serial.print()`.
what is char array strings in arduino | arduino char array strings | how does char array strings work in arduino code => Text strings can be represented in two ways. you can use the String data type, or you can make a string out of an array of type char and null-terminate it.
what is the string object in arduino | arduino the string object | how does the string object work in arduino code => Constructs an instance of the String class.
what is unsigned char in arduino | arduino unsigned char | how does unsigned char work in arduino code => An unsigned data type that occupies 1 byte of memory. Same as the `byte` datatype. The unsigned char datatype encodes numbers from 0 to 255. For consistency of Arduino programming style, the `byte` data type is to be preferred.
what is void in arduino | arduino void | how does void work in arduino code => The `void` keyword is used only in function declarations. It indicates that the function is expected to return no information to the function from which it was called.
what is const in arduino | arduino const | how does const work in arduino code => The `const` keyword stands for constant. It is a variable qualifier that modifies the behavior of the variable, making a variable "read-only". This means that the variable can be used just as any other variable of its type, but its value cannot be changed.
what is variable scope in arduino | arduino variable scope | how does variable scope work in arduino code => Variables in the C++ programming language, which Arduino uses, have a property called scope. This is in contrast to early versions of languages such as BASIC where every variable is a global variable. A global variable is one that can be seen by every function in a program.
what is static in arduino | arduino static | how does static work in arduino code => The `static` keyword is used to create variables that are visible to only one function. However unlike local variables that get created and destroyed every time a function is called, static variables persist beyond the function call, preserving their data between function calls.
what is volatile in arduino | arduino volatile | how does volatile work in arduino code => In Arduino, `volatile` is a keyword known as a variable qualifier, it is usually used before the datatype of a variable, to modify the way in which the compiler and subsequent program treat the variable. Declaring a variable `volatile` is a directive to the compiler.
what is progmem in arduino | arduino progmem | how does progmem work in arduino code => Keep constant data in flash (program) memory only, instead of copying it to SRAM when the program starts.
what is sizeof in arduino | arduino sizeof | how does sizeof work in arduino code => The `sizeof` operator returns the number of bytes in a variable type, or the number of bytes occupied by an array.
what is setup in arduino | arduino setup | how does setup work in arduino code => The `setup()` function is called when a sketch starts. Use it to initialize variables, pin modes, start using libraries, and so on. The `setup()` function will only run once, after each powerup or reset of the Arduino board.
what is loop in arduino | arduino loop | how does loop work in arduino code => After creating a `setup()` function, which initializes and sets the initial values, the `loop()` function does precisely what its name suggests, and loops consecutively, allowing your program to change and respond. Use it to actively control the Arduino board.
what is break in arduino | arduino break | how does break work in arduino code => In Arduino, `break` is used to exit from a `for`, `while` or `do...while` loop, bypassing the normal loop condition. It is also used to exit from a `switch case` statement.
what is do while in arduino | arduino do while | how does do while work in arduino code => The `do...while` loop works in the same manner as the `while` loop, with the exception that the condition is tested at the end of the loop, so the do loop will always run at least once.
what is else in arduino | arduino else | how does else work in arduino code => The `if...else` allows greater control over the flow of code than the basic `if` statement, by allowing multiple tests to be grouped. An `else` clause (if at all exists) will be executed if the condition in the `if` statement results in `false`.
what is for in arduino | arduino for | how does for work in arduino code => The `for` statement is used to repeat a block of statements enclosed in curly braces. An increment counter is usually used to increment and terminate the loop.
what is goto in arduino | arduino goto | how does goto work in arduino code => Transfers program flow to a labeled point in the program.
what is if in arduino | arduino if => The `if` statement checks for a condition and executes the following statement or set of statements if the condition is 'true'.
what is return in arduino | arduino return | how does return work in arduino code => Terminate a function and return a value from a function to the calling function, if desired.
what is switch case in arduino | arduino switch case | how does switch case work in arduino code => Like if statements, switch case controls the flow of programs by allowing programmers to specify different code that should be executed in various conditions. In particular, a switch statement compares the value of a variable to the values specified in case statements.
what is #define in arduino | arduino #define | how does #define work in arduino code => In Arduino, `#define` is a useful C++ component that allows the programmer to give a name to a constant value before the program is compiled. Defined constants in arduino don't take up any program memory space on the chip.
what is #include in arduino | arduino #include | how does #include work in arduino code => In Arduino, `#include` is used to include outside libraries in your sketch. This gives the programmer access to a large group of standard C libraries (groups of pre-made functions), and also libraries written especially for Arduino.
what is block comments in arduino | arduino block comments | how does block comments work in arduino code => Comments are lines in the program that are used to inform yourself or others about the way the program works. They are ignored by the compiler, and not exported to the processor, so they don't take up any space in the microcontroller's flash memory.
what is semicolon in arduino | arduino semicolon | how does semicolon work in arduino code => Used to end a statement.
what is curly braces in arduino | arduino curly braces | how does curly braces work in arduino code => Curly braces (also referred to as just "braces" or as "curly brackets") are a major part of the C++ programming language.
